title: French meridian arc of Delambre and Méchain, Dunkerque to Barcelona
region: Dunkerque to Montjoui (Barcelona) along the meridian of Paris
summary: Delambre measured the northern part of the chain from Dunkerque to Rodez and Méchain the southern part from Rodez to Barcelona, from 1792 to 1798. Both used repeating circles of Borda, divided in grades, and observed each angle in series of many repetitions. A special commission fixed one value for each angle from the series. Volume 1 (1806) prints these values in the Tableau général des triangles (pp. 513-542), with the register page, the spherical excess, and the spherical angles closed by one third of the error. Two bases were measured with Borda's platinum rules in 1798: Melun (6075.90 toises) and Perpignan (6006.25 toises). Volume 2 (1807) prints the Tableau complet des triangles (pp. 800-839) with the side lengths in toises and metres; volume 3 (1810) gives the arc lengths, the degree lengths and the metre.

steps.text: Each angle was measured with a repeating circle of Borda in series of 10 to 80 repetitions. Delambre's circles were no. 1 (radius 0.21 m) and no. 4 (0.18 m), divided into 400 grades of 10 parts each. Each series was reduced to the centre of the station.
steps.instrument: Repeating circles of Borda no. 1 and no. 4 (Delambre), no. 2 and no. 3 (Méchain)
steps.quote: Les deux cercles avec lesquels j'ai fait toutes mes observations avoient de rayon, l'un 0m21, et l'autre 0m18. Le plus grand étoit marqué du n° 1, le second du n° 4. Méchain avoit les nos 2 et 3. Les deux miens étoient divisés en quatre cents degrés subdivisés chacun en dix parties

steps.text: The register gives each series reduced to the centre, the mean of the series, the reduction to the horizon, and the angle at the horizon (the spherical angle). The commission then fixed one value; at Dunkerque it kept 42 6 9.34, close to the first series, instead of the mean 42 6 8.81.
steps.quote: Réduction à l'horizon . . . - 0"86. Angle à l'horizon ou angle sphérique . . . 42° 6' 8"81. En se rapprochant de la première série, qui est la meilleure . . . 42° 6' 9"34. C'est à ce dernier résultat que s'est arrêtée la commission spéciale nommée pour examiner les observations.

steps.text: The excess of each angle (the difference between the spherical angle and the angle of the chords) was taken from tables V and VI of the preliminary discourse, built on a degree of 57020 toises. The sum of the three was compared with the excess of the whole triangle.
steps.quote: Cet excès a été calculé par les tables qui sont à la suite du discours préliminaire.

steps.text: The closing error of each triangle (observed sum minus 180 degrees minus the excess) was given in equal thirds to the three angles. These are the 'angles sphériques' of vol. 1. For vol. 2, Delambre changed the angles of triangles 44 to 100 by 0.01 to 0.1 second so that the Melun base, carried through the chain, gives the Perpignan base.
steps.quote: les angles sphériques tels qu'on les a donnés tom. I, p. 513 et suiv.; c'est-à-dire corrigés du tiers de la somme des trois erreurs.

steps.text: Melun base (Lieursaint to Melun): measured with the four platinum rules of Borda from 5 floréal to 15 prairial an 6, in 45 days; arc 6075.89730 toises, adopted 6075.90. Perpignan base (Vernet to Salces): measure begun 19 thermidor an 6; arc 6006.25545, adopted 6006.25.
steps.instrument: Four platinum rules of Borda, two toises long, each with a copper rule as a metallic thermometer
steps.quote: La mesure de la base a commencé le 5 floréal (24 mai 1798); elle a continué sans un seul jour d'interruption, et elle a été terminée le 15 prairial (3 juin), après quarante-cinq jours de travail.

steps.text: Sides were computed with log sines of the spherical angles (Vlacq's 10-place tables), the sine of the first side taken as unit and later scaled on the Melun base. All work was done in logarithms; the arcs and chords in toises and the metres are printed for the reader.
steps.quote: Tous ces nombres de toises ou de mètres ne sont là que pour la curiosité du lecteur. Tous les calculs ont été faits sur les logarithmes, sans y faire entrer aucun nombre.

steps.text: Latitudes at Dunkerque, Paris (Panthéon), Évaux, Carcassonne and Montjoui from zenith distances of the Pole Star and other circumpolar stars with the repeating circle. See astro.json.

angle_status.text: angles_observed_deg are the 'Angles observés' column of the Tableau général des triangles (vol. 1, pp. 513-542). These are the values that the special commission fixed from the station registers: means of the repeated series, reduced to the centre of the station and to the horizon. The commission sometimes dropped or favoured a series (notes 39, 49, 70, 72 of the Tableau), and at Bastide (triangles 86, 87) 1.3 seconds was taken off from the observations of p. 277. No closing correction is in them: their sum differs from 180 degrees plus the excess by the printed 'Somme des erreurs'. The next column, 'Angles sphériques', is the observed angle plus one third of that error, so it closes exactly on 180 degrees plus the computed excess. Vol. 2 (Tableau complet, pp. 800-839) prints these closed spherical angles, further changed by 0.01 to 0.1 second in triangles 44 to 100 to make the two bases agree (p. 704). Neither the vol. 1 spherical angles nor the vol. 2 angles are used for sums here. Where one angle of a triangle is marked '*' in the Pages column, it was not observed but concluded from the other two, and the sum is forced; those triangles have sum_minus_180_arcsec null.
angle_status.source: Delambre & Méchain (1806), vol. 1, pp. 511-512; Delambre & Méchain (1807), vol. 2, pp. 699-700, 704
angle_status.quote: La quatrième offre les angles tels qu'ils ont été arrêtés par la commission spéciale chargée d'examiner nos registres. [...] La sixième contient les angles sphériques corrigés pour le calcul. (vol. 2, p. 704:) Dans le triangle 44 j'ai retranché 0"1 à l'angle de Torfou, et ajouté 0"05 à chacun des deux autres.

excess_formula.text: E = 0"00004.831 (AB)^2 sin 2A + 0"00004.831 (BC)^2 sin 2C (sides in toises; printed coefficient 4.831 x 10^-9 arcsec per square toise, CALC reading of the printed figure grouping), which Delambre shows equals 4a times the area of the plane triangle (0"00009.662 times twice the area). The coefficient comes from a degree of 57020 toises, that is a sphere of radius 3 267 005 toises = 6367.5 km (CALC). Tables V and VI of the preliminary discourse give the excess from two sides and an angle, or from base and height on the triangle map.
excess_formula.quote: (A + B + C - 180°) = 0"00004.831 (AB)². sin. 2A + 0"00004.831 (BC)². sin. 2C [...] = 4 a. surface du triangle considéré comme rectiligne.

side_formula.text: Sine rule on the spherical triangle with 10-place log sines of the spherical angles (Vlacq); the sides come out as log sines of the arcs, changed to log arcs with table II of vol. 2. Scale: Melun base for Dunkerque to Évaux, carried on to Perpignan after the angle changes of triangles 44 to 100. Arcs in toises at the height of the signals are not reduced to sea level in the arc column; the metre column uses 1 toise = 1.949036591 m.
side_formula.quote: Les sinus des côtés opposés que présente la sixième colonne sont calculés d'après les angles corrigés comme nous venons de dire

assumptions.text: The excess is computed for a sphere with a degree of 57020 toises.
The closing error of each triangle is shared in equal thirds among its three angles.
assumptions.quote: corrigés du tiers de la somme des trois erreurs

assumptions.text: The angles of triangles 44 to 100 are changed by up to 0.1 second so that the two bases agree; the bases are held more certain than the angles.
assumptions.quote: faire disparoître la différence entre les deux bases que je crois plus certaines encore que nos angles

assumptions.text: The toise is half of rule no. I (the module) at its standard temperature.
assumptions.quote: Ces bases sont exprimées en toises qui sont la moitié de la règle n° I

assumptions.text: 1 toise = 1.949036591 m: the commission's quarter meridian is 5130740 toises and the metre is its ten-millionth part (CALC 10^7 / 5130740).
assumptions.quote: Le nombre adopté par la commission est . . . 5130740

error_figures.value: about one pouce on a base of 6000 toises
error_figures.quote: L'incertitude que nous examinons en ce moment ne monte donc guère qu'à un pouce, en mettant tout au pis

error_figures.what: closing error of each triangle ('Somme des erreurs')
error_figures.value: printed per triangle in vol. 1, pp. 513-542; from -3.45" (triangle 23) to +4.69" (triangles 20 and 72)
